vsam.why: base/cntl/adef121.jcl DEFINE1: DATA(... KEYS(10 0) RECORDSIZE(225 225)); the engine's facts do not read KEYS / RECORDSIZE inside the DATA component, so the case states them

region.why: a deployment fact: LGICVS01 ASSIGNs SYSID (unused afterwards); GenApp names no region in the corpus

scenarios.name: link-key-on-file
scenarios.why: LINKed with STARTCODE D: LOW = HIGH = 3: the key is 0000000003, on file; READ GTEQ reads it (NORMAL) and SEND TEXT shows HIGH CUSTOMER=0000000003; the key goes back in COMMA-DATA (no SEND TEXT)

scenarios.name: link-next-key
scenarios.why: LINKed with STARTCODE D: the key 0000000011 is not on file: GTEQ reads the first greater key, 0001000005 (NORMAL), and its number is sent; the key goes back in COMMA-DATA (no SEND TEXT)

scenarios.name: link-past-the-end
scenarios.why: LINKed with STARTCODE D: no key >= 0002000000: NOTFND (RESP2 80); WRITE-MSG-HIGH keeps the key asked for; the key goes back in COMMA-DATA (no SEND TEXT)

scenarios.name: link-random-in-range
scenarios.why: LINKed with STARTCODE D: LOW 1, HIGH 10: the key is FUNCTION RANDOM(EIBTASKN) scaled into the range (C12, X21), read by GTEQ; the key goes back in COMMA-DATA (no SEND TEXT)

scenarios.name: link-queue-empty
scenarios.why: LINKed with STARTCODE D: no GENACNTL queue: the first ReadQ is not NORMAL, WS-FLAG-TSQE stays 'Y' and the E, L and H records are all written; LOW = HIGH = 0001000001 (the program's defaults), the key is read by GTEQ

scenarios.name: link-queue-header-only
scenarios.why: LINKed with STARTCODE D: GENACNTL holds only the header item: the first ReadQ is NORMAL (TSQE cleared) but no LOW CUSTOMER or HIGH CUSTOMER item follows, so the L and H records are written; LOW = HIGH = 0001000001

scenarios.name: link-queue-low-only
scenarios.why: LINKed with STARTCODE D: no HIGH CUSTOMER item: LOW is taken from the queue, HIGH keeps its default, so only the H record is written; the key is scaled into LOW..HIGH

scenarios.name: link-queue-high-only
scenarios.why: LINKed with STARTCODE D: no LOW CUSTOMER item: HIGH is taken from the queue, LOW keeps its default, so only the L record is written; the key is scaled into LOW..HIGH

scenarios.name: terminal-start-on-linked-case
scenarios.why: STARTCODE TD with no COMMAREA and no invoking program: WS-FLAG is 'R', the RECEIVE runs and SEND TEXT shows HIGH CUSTOMER=0000000003; the other arm of the STARTCODE test than the LINKed scenarios take

notes: GenApp's VSAM 'customer key range' inquiry LGICVS01 as a distributed program link (the COMMAREA sibling of genapp-lgicvs01, which covers the terminal path). No GenApp program LINKs LGICVS01, so the program's own test for a called run -- IF WS-STARTCODE(1:1) = 'D' or WS-Invokeprog Not = Spaces -- is reached by STARTCODE 'D' (IBM: a task started for a distributed program link; X19), the one fact a harness can state without a calling program in the corpus. The branch sets WS-FLAG 'C', copies COMMA-DATA to WS-COMMAREA and EIBCALEN to WS-RECV-LEN, and does no RECEIVE; the TS queue GENACNTL read, the random key and the READ FILE('KSDSCUST') GTEQ are the terminal case's. At the end WS-FLAG is not 'R', so the answer goes back into COMMA-DATA ('HIGH CUSTOMER=' and the 10-digit key) and the task RETURNs with no SEND TEXT. Queue-shape scenarios (queue-empty, queue-header-only, queue-low-only, queue-high-only, link- prefixed): a queue with a missing item makes the program WRITEQ 'LOW CUSTOMER=' / 'HIGH CUSTOMER=' FROM(WRITE-MSG-L / -H) X(13) / X(14) LENGTH(23) / (24), past its FROM item (X6: written padded, FROM's bytes then spaces, ASSUMED on both sides), so each task is compared whole. They reach the ReadQ-not-NORMAL and the LOW / HIGH not-found sides. Not exercised: the non-blank INVOKINGPROG arm of that test (it needs a calling program; the STARTCODE arm takes the same statements). Data: ksdscust.txt is the genapp-lgicvs01 case's (ten GenApp sample customers plus two SYNTHETIC ones).
